summary: William Jones was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Harrow School, University College, Oxford, Middle Temple, and under Ram Chand and others. He founded The Asiatic Society and served as Chief Justice at Fort William and judge at Calcutta High Court.

William Joseph Wilkins worked in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Highgate School and Hackney College, he taught at Bhowanipore Missionary Institution and Bhownipur College for the London Missionary Society from around 1870 to 1884.

William Knighton was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. His career included serving as headmaster at Norman Seminary in Colombo (~1845–1849), Lecturer in History and Logic at Presidency University in 1846, and a post in the Indian Civil Service.

William L. Ames is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He earned an M.S. at Caltech and a Ph.D. at the University of Washington under Collett Cox and David Seyfort Ruegg, later serving as a librarian at John F. Kennedy University.

William Lee-Warner was an Indology and history scholar who studied at Rugby School and St John's College. He served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1869 to 1895 and was a Fellow of the University of Mumbai.

William Linwood was an Indologist and linguist educated at Christ Church, Oxford. He served as a teacher at Shrewsbury School (~1841–1842) and as a public examiner at the University of Oxford in 1850.

William Logan worked in Indology, history, and archaeology after studying at the University of Edinburgh. He served in the Madras Civil Service from 1862 to 1888 and became a Fellow of the University of Madras in 1882.

William M. Bodiford is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. Educated at Kansas, Yale, Tsukuba, and Komazawa, he taught at Meiji Gakuin, Davidson, Iowa, and UCLA, where he became Professor Emeritus.

William M. Gorvine is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his B.A. at Connecticut College and his M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Virginia, completing his doctorate under David Germano.
William MacColin Kirkpatrick was an Indologist who was educated at Bishop Cotton School and served in the Indian Civil Service.

William Markby worked in Indology and law. Educated at Merton College and Oxford, he was Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta (~1877–1878), Reader in Indian Law at Oxford (1878–1900), and Curator of the Indian Institute (1884–1910).

William McCulloch was an Indologist and scholar of religion who studied at the Royal High School, Addiscombe Military Seminary, George Watson's College, and the University of Edinburgh. In 1886, he served as Principal of Chinsurah Theological College.

William McGrath is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his MA-PhD at the University of Virginia (2010–2017) and was appointed Assistant Professor at New York University in 2021.

William Montgomery McGovern was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Christ Church, Oxford, Berlin, and Paris, he held posts at SOAS (1918–1924), Field Museum of Natural History (1927), and Northwestern University (from 1929).

William Nassau Lees was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and history who studied at Trinity College Dublin. He served as Principal and Professor at Aliah University (~1853–1870) and Secretary to the Board of Examiners at Fort William (~1855–1870).
William P. Chu is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of California, Los Angeles, and studied there under doctoral supervisor Robert E. Buswell Jr.

William Pettigrew was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Ardington Aborigines Mission Training Centre (~1888–1890). In 1894, he served as a missionary with the American Baptist Missionary Union.

William Price was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He served on Gore Ouseley's Mission to Persia (1811–1812) and taught at Fort William College, where he was appointed Professor of Hindee and Hindoostanee in 1824.

William R. Hutchison was a scholar of religious studies and history who studied at Oxford and Yale. He taught at Yale, Hunter College, American University, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and Harvard University.

William R. LaFleur was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Calvin University, Michigan, and Chicago, he taught at Princeton, UCLA, and the University of Pennsylvania, where he was Professor in Japanese Studies (~1990–2010).
